display.title: Episode 294: The Dancing Bear (Yomim Noraim)
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi's last show before Rosh Hashanah 5748: the meaning of the Days of Awe, and how the Shpoler Zeide, taught by Eliyahu HaNavi, out-danced a cruel poritz to free a prisoner.
display.summary_long: Broadcast two days before Rosh Hashanah 5748. Uncle Yossi explains why the Ten Days of Teshuvah are called the Days of Awe: Hashem decides our life, health and livelihood for the coming year, so we are careful not to go against His will and return through teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah. When we crown Him as our Father and King and the shofar sounds, Hashem moves from the Throne of Judgment to the Throne of Mercy. He urges children to find out when shofar is blown in their shul. After the Hakochainik march, sung to 'Achakeh lo', and the Shema with a young yeshiva student, he tells a story for the Shpoler Zeide's yahrzeit on Vov Tishrei. Asked by Rabbi Avraham HaMalach where he learned to dance so well, the Shpoler Zeide explains that Eliyahu HaNavi sent him to rescue a Jew held by a cruel poritz who made prisoners dance in a bearskin and threw the losers to the dogs. He took the prisoner's place, and his dancing freed him. The show closes with the new Tzivos Hashem newsletter, Tishrei mitzvah charts, a Sukkos event and New Year wishes.
display.lesson: In the Days of Awe we crown Hashem as King and return to Him; and serving Him with joy, even dancing, to save another Jew can be worth more than prayer.

date.note: Consistent with the audio: 'right before the Yomim Noraim'; New Year wishes at the end.

advisories.note: A cruel poritz jails Jews who cannot pay rent and forces prisoners to dance in a bearskin.
Prisoners who lose the dance are thrown to hungry dogs (told, not shown).
The tzaddik gives a guard whiskey until he falls asleep in order to free a prisoner.
Hashem judges each person's life for the coming year during the Days of Awe.

privacy.note: A studio guest and three sisters pictured in the newsletter are named in full.

sources_cited.note: 'Our Chachamim tell us': at the sound of the shofar Hashem rises from the Throne of Judgment to the Throne of Mercy.
